learn.hook: Can you find 103 × 103 in your head in five seconds? With the right identity, you can!
points: An identity is an equality that is true for every value of the variables, unlike an equation such as x + 2 = 5, which is true for only one value.
(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². Picture a square of side a + b split into an a × a square, a b × b square and two a × b rectangles.

steps: 103 = 100 + 3, so use (a + b)² with a = 100, b = 3

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers who multiply mentally often use these tricks: 49 × 51 = 50² − 1² = 2499.

games.title: Match each product with its expansion

quiz.mistake: Forgets the middle term 2ab and writes x² + 49
Forgets to double the middle term (getting 9804) or drops the + b² (getting 9600)
Adds 9 instead of subtracting it
Forgets to double the middle term, writing 6ab

quiz.explain: Use (x + a)(x + b) with a = 4, b = −9: a + b = −5 and ab = −36.
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign of the middle term wrong

quiz.q: If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, find a² + b².
quiz.explain: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab, so a² + b² = 100 − 42 = 58. Check with a = 3, b = 7: 9 + 49 = 58.
quiz.mistake: Takes a² + b² = (a + b)², forgetting the 2ab

quiz.q: Which of these is an identity (true for every value of x)?
quiz.explain: (x + 1)² = x² + 2x + 1 holds for every x. The others are true only for some values (or are false in general).
quiz.mistake: Confuses an equation that is true for one value with an identity
Uses only a − b and forgets to multiply by a + b

teach.ask: Gappu groans: "Why isn't (a + b)² just a² + b²? That looks so much simpler!"
teach.praise: Of course! The big square also has two a × b rectangles, so (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² for every value. I won't forget 2ab now!
teach.nudge: If you draw a square of side a + b, what pieces do you see besides a² and b²?

learn.hook: 11³ = 1331 and 101³ = 1030301. Patterns like these come straight from the cube identities!
points: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b) = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³.
(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b) = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³.
a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).
a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). So if a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.
learn.reallife: Volumes of cube-shaped boxes grow as a cube. If each side of a 10 cm box grows by 1 cm, (a + b)³ shows exactly how much extra space you get.

games.title: Cube check
items: You also need the term 3ab(a + b). Try a = b = 1: 8 is not 2.
Multiply out the right side and the middle terms cancel, leaving a³ − b³.
If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc
This follows from a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(...), which is 0 when a + b + c = 0.
Use (a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³ with a = x, b = 1.

quiz.explain: a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ with a = x, b = 2 gives x³ + 6x² + 12x + 8.
quiz.mistake: Cubes each term separately and drops the middle terms
Uses 3ab instead of 3ab(a + b), getting 1000608, or forgets the middle part entirely

quiz.explain: −12 + 7 + 5 = 0, so the sum of cubes equals 3abc = 3 × (−12) × 7 × 5 = −1260.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is 0 because a + b + c = 0, or drops the negative sign

quiz.explain: Use a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca with c = 2: 2bc = 4y and 2ca = 4x.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the cross terms

quiz.explain: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) with a = x, b = 3.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the signs of the sum-of-cubes and difference-of-cubes identities

quiz.q: If x + y = 5 and xy = 6, find x³ + y³.
quiz.mistake: Thinks x³ + y³ = (x + y)³

quiz.explain: (a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³ with a = 2x, b = 1: 8x³ − 12x² + 6x − 1.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to cube the 2 in 2x, or gets the alternating signs wrong

quiz.q: If a + b + c = 9 and ab + bc + ca = 26, find a² + b² + c².
quiz.explain: a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca) = 81 − 52 = 29.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 26 instead of 2 × 26

teach.ask: Gappu counts on his feathers: "Why does (a + b)³ have so many terms? Can't I just cube a and cube b?"
teach.praise: (a + b)³ is (a + b) multiplied three times, so the extra terms 3a²b + 3ab² appear. Just a³ + b³ is not enough!
teach.nudge: What do you get if you multiply (a + b)² by (a + b) once more?

learn.hook: Expanding is like opening a gift box; factorising is packing it back. Identities show you how the box was folded!
points: To factorise means to write an expression as a product of simpler expressions.
Always take out a common factor first: 3x² − 75 = 3(x² − 25).
Look for patterns: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b); a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)²; a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)².
For x² + px + q, find two numbers with sum p and product q: x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4).
a³ + b³ and a³ − b³ have their own factor forms. Always check by expanding your answer.

steps: Middle term: 2 × 2x × 3 = 12x, with a minus sign
So it matches a² − 2ab + b² with a = 2x, b = 3

learn.reallife: If a rectangular rangoli has area x² + 9x + 20, factorising tells you possible side lengths: (x + 4) and (x + 5).

games.title: Match each expression with its factors
Factorise 3x² − 75
items: Spot a difference of squares: x² − 5²

quiz.explain: 9y² − 16 = (3y)² − 4², a difference of squares.
quiz.mistake: Writes a difference of squares as a perfect square
Finds numbers with product 16 but ignores the sum 8

quiz.explain: We need two numbers with sum −7 and product 12: −3 and −4.
quiz.mistake: Uses + signs even though the middle term is negative

quiz.explain: Take out 2 to get 2(x² − 9), then x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).
quiz.mistake: Stops after taking out the common factor
Computes (87 − 13)² = 5476 instead

quiz.explain: Two numbers with product −20 and sum +1 are 5 and −4.
quiz.mistake: Puts the signs the wrong way round, giving a sum of −1
Uses a minus sign in the second bracket, mixing it up with a³ + b³

quiz.q: A rectangular rangoli has area x² + 9x + 20 square units. One side is (x + 4). What is the other side?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 4 from 20 instead of dividing, or uses the coefficient 9

teach.ask: Gappu stares at x² − 49: "How do I break this into factors? Where do I start?"
teach.praise: First take out anything common, then match a pattern like a² − b², and finally multiply back to check. x² − 49 = (x − 7)(x + 7)!
teach.nudge: Is 49 a square number? Which identity has a minus sign between two squares?
